ai.description: *Gongylosoma frenatum* is a slender, 30–40 cm snake with a brown dorsum and a distinct dark lateral stripe extending from the snout through the eye. It features a pale, unspotted yellow-white belly.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Gongylosoma frenatum* is the presence of a distinct, dark lateral stripe running from the snout through the eye along the neck.
ai.habitat: *Gongylosoma frenatum* typically inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, often found in leaf litter at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The stripe-necked snake is primarily diurnal and actively hunts for small skinks and other lizards among leaf litter and low vegetation during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Gongylosoma frenatum* is oviparous, typically laying a small clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding generally occurs during the monsoon season, between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: Gongylosoma frenatum occurs in the Western Ghats of India, primarily in Kerala and Tamil Nadu, ranging from lowlands up to approximately 1,200 meters in elevation.
